artifact_inventory.description: Deterministic NumPy checks of the normal spectral-filter bound, the exact two-eigenvalue sharpness formula, the power-iteration corollary, and the exact-zero example.
Verified output of the deterministic numerical checks, including Python and NumPy versions needed to reproduce the floating-point sanity checks.

limitations: Exact arithmetic, finite-dimensional normal matrices, exact spectral-filter application, and Euclidean Rayleigh residual for the main theorem. Nonnormal matrices, finite-precision and inexact filter evaluation, and complete filtered eigensolvers with orthogonalization or Rayleigh-Ritz extraction are outside the one-step law. Relative amplification may be unbounded only as the input residual tends to zero; no absolute blow-up is claimed. The minimax filter-design statement does not constrain polynomial degree, rational poles, or evaluation cost. Older spectral-transformation, simultaneous-iteration, and general variance-comparison literature leaves residual historical-equivalence risk.
record_title: Sharp Rayleigh-residual distortion under normal spectral filtering
scientific_context: For a normal matrix, normalized application of a nonvanishing spectral filter changes spectral weights by squared filter gains. The exact worst-case one-step amplification of the standard Rayleigh residual is the filter gain dynamic range M/m. This yields an exact universal residual-nonexpansiveness classification, a zero-gain dichotomy, and a sharp minimax reciprocal tradeoff: any nonvanishing filter with wanted/unwanted separation factor eta<1 admits worst-case Rayleigh-residual amplification at least 1/eta, and the bound is attainable by two-level gain filters.
